title: Appliance Extended Warranties: Why They are NOT Worth it?
summary: An appliance retailer argues most extended warranties aren't worth it because stores lack in-house service and route claims through third parties, while pitching its own serviced warranty as the exception.

assertions.quote: appliances without service sell the warranty to a third party. The third party company is responsible for fixing your appliance.

verdicts.note: Most big-box and online appliance retailers lack in-house service departments and route warranty service through third-party contract administrators.

assertions.quote: fewer than 5% of all appliance stores, even the high end ones, have a service department

verdicts.note: This specific figure is a self-reported claim from one retailer, not independently verified industry data, though the general pattern is plausible.

assertions.quote: all those people have retired and there are even few people learning the trade

verdicts.note: An aging, shrinking appliance-repair workforce is a widely reported industry trend that lengthens service wait times.

assertions.quote: you'll be caught in endless finger pointing

verdicts.note: Diffusing responsibility across unrelated parties commonly produces the finger-pointing pattern consumers report in reviews of third-party administered warranties.

assertions.quote: They sold you the warranty and have the resources to fix the issues.

verdicts.note: Vertically integrated service does remove one layer of finger-pointing, but it does not guarantee good service or claim approval on its own.

assertions.quote: Typically, an extended warranty is less expensive than a service call.

verdicts.note: A warranty's price can be lower than one repair bill, but this ignores that many covered appliances never need a paid repair during the term, so it's not a clear average win.

assertions.quote: In most cases, you should not buy a warranty because most don't provide adequate coverage.

verdicts.note: Analyses of extended warranty economics generally find the expected payout is below the premium for most buyers, supporting the gist, though it depends heavily on appliance type and reliability.
CR opens by warning that whatever you spend on a service plan for a laptop, dishwasher, or car is likely money down the drain, i.e. not worth the coverage for most buyers.
